punchline: The mushroom we see is only a small tip of the fungus, and hidden threads beneath it hold ecosystems together.
thirty_sec: Merlin Sheldrake says fungi are neither plants nor animals but a kingdom of their own, genetically closer to animals. A mushroom is only the fruiting body. Below it runs a web of fine threads called mycelium, which trades minerals with plant roots and breaks down dead matter. The book is Entangled Life.
